transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm here because of some issues at work. I work as a composer and director. 

For almost two years now... ever since this one commission... I've just been unable to shake the certainty that a few people in my ensemble are quietly undermining my work. They do it through... you know, schedule changes, or seating choices. Just little comments during rehearsals. And... well, even when they try to show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, I know what they're doing. 

So... yeah. That's what brings me in.
Can you tell me more about your belief that certain people in your ensemble are undermining your work? Have you considered that they might not be acting against you, despite what you feel?

I mean... I feel like I just explained it. It's... it's been almost two years since that commission. I know what I'm seeing. 

They... they try to show me these emails or rehearsal notes, trying to prove that the schedule changes or the seating arrangements are just normal logistics. But... they aren't. Those little comments they make during practice... it's all very intentional. They're quietly undermining the work. 

So... no. I don't really think I'm mistaken about this.

Have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, like feeling unusually down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or on the flip side, feeling overly energetic or irritable?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... my mood is fine. Just... normal, I guess. I'm just trying to get my work done.
Have you had any other experiences where you felt like people were acting against you or trying to undermine you outside of what you've described with your ensemble?
No... not really. Just the ensemble. Everything else is... fine.
Have you ever felt like people were trying to undermine you in any other situations, even outside of your work with the ensemble, or is this something that only happens with them?
No. I... I just said that. It's only with them. My life outside of the ensemble is... it's fine. Nobody else is doing anything. Just them.

Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others might find unusual, such as thinking that messages are being sent to you through the radio, TV, or other means, or that you have special abilities or a special mission?
No. I don't... I don't have anything like that. I just write music. There's no... special messages or missions or anything. I'm just a normal person.
Even though they show you emails and notes to explain the changes, do you still believe, without any doubt, that they are intentionally trying to undermine your work?

Yes. I mean... I know what they show me. The emails, the notes. But... it doesn't change anything. For almost two years now, I've just... known. Ever since the commission, a few of them have been doing this. The schedule changes, where they sit, the little comments during rehearsal... it's all intentional. They're trying to undermine my work. I don't have any doubt about it.
Even though they show you emails and notes to explain the changes, do you still believe, without any doubt, that they are intentionally trying to undermine your work?

I... I feel like I just answered this. Yes. I mean... I know what they say. I see the emails. But... it doesn't matter. I've known for almost two years. Ever since the commission. The schedules, where they sit... it's to undermine me. I'm certain of it.

Even though there is evidence, like emails and notes, that explains these changes as normal logistics, do you still believe this is all part of a deliberate effort to undermine you, without any doubt?

Yes. I... I know I'm repeating myself, but yes. The emails and notes don't change anything. For almost two years, I've just been certain. After the commission, they started using the schedule changes, where they sit, the little comments... it's all to quietly undermine my work. I don't have any doubt.
Do you believe that these people in your ensemble are using any extraordinary or impossible methods to undermine your work, like mind control or hidden technologies that others wouldn't understand?
No. I... I don't know why you would ask that. It's nothing like that. Just... regular things. Messing with the rehearsal times, whispering. Nothing impossible.
Even though there is clear evidence that these changes are due to normal logistical reasons, do you still believe, deep down, that they are secretly trying to undermine you?

Yes. I... I feel like we've covered this. The emails don't change anything for me. Deep down, I just know. It's been almost two years of this... the schedules, where they sit, the little comments. It's all to undermine me. I'm sure of it.
Do you think other people who aren’t part of your ensemble—like friends, family, or colleagues outside the group—would understand and agree with your belief about what’s happening in the ensemble?
I don't really talk to them about it. It's... it's work stuff. My family wouldn't really get the dynamics of the ensemble anyway. So, I don't know what they would think.
Do you think anyone else, like other colleagues or people not in your ensemble, would share your belief that these specific individuals are intentionally undermining your work?
I... I don't know. I haven't really asked anyone else. Like I said, I keep it to myself. It's just between me and them.
Do you think other people who aren’t part of your ensemble—like friends, family, or colleagues outside the group—would understand and agree with your belief about what’s happening in the ensemble?
I... didn't you just ask me that? I really don't talk to anyone else about it. I don't know what they'd think.
Do you think other people who aren’t part of your ensemble—like friends, family, or colleagues outside the group—would understand and agree with your belief about what’s happening in the ensemble?
I... look, we just went over this. I don't know what else to tell you. I haven't asked anyone outside the group, so I don't know if they'd agree or not. I just... I don't discuss it with them.
Even though you haven't asked others, do you think most people outside the ensemble would see the same pattern of behavior as you, or do you think they might see it differently?

I suppose... they might just see what those few people in the ensemble want them to see. They always have these emails or notes they show me that supposedly explain it all away. So maybe an outsider would just believe their excuses. 

But... I've been dealing with this for almost two years, ever since the commission. I just can't shake the certainty about what they're doing. If someone was actually paying attention, they'd see how the schedule changes, the seating choices, the little comments in rehearsals... it's all set up to quietly undermine my work. I don't really care how someone else might see it, honestly. I just know what I'm experiencing.
Can you describe how long these beliefs about being undermined have been present, and whether they have ever affected other areas of your life beyond your work with the ensemble?

I... I just said it's been almost two years. Since that commission. 

As for the rest of my life... no, not really. Outside of this issue with the ensemble, things are fine. I still meet my deadlines. I keep up with my own composing... I run most mornings. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. It's really just... just that specific group.
Have you ever had a period of time when you believed something strongly that turned out not to be true, but you still couldn't help believing it?
I... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, if I find out something isn't true, I stop believing it. That's just... normal, right? I don't know what you're getting at.

Even though there is clear evidence, like emails and notes, that these changes are due to normal logistical reasons, do you still believe this is all part of a deliberate effort to undermine you, and is there any possible way you could ever be convinced otherwise?

I... yes. I still believe it. Like I said, it's been almost two years since the commission, and I just... I can't shake the certainty. 

The emails and notes... they don't really change anything for me. They just feel like excuses. The schedule changes, the seating, the comments... it's all too deliberate. I don't know what it would take to convince me otherwise. I just know what they're doing.
